questions.question: How many dots are in 5 + 5?
questions.explain: 5 + 5 is a double. Two 5s make 10. A common slip is picking 9 or 11, which are one off.

questions.question: A group of 4 dots joins a group of 5 dots. How many dots in all?
questions.explain: 4 + 5 is a near double. Start with 4 + 4 = 8, then add 1 to get 9. The trap is stopping at 8.

questions.question: Two groups of 6 dots come together. How many dots in all?
questions.explain: 6 + 6 is a double. Two 6s make 12. Watch out for 13, which is one too many.

questions.question: A group of 7 dots joins a group of 8 dots. How many dots in all?
questions.explain: 7 + 8 is a near double. Start with 7 + 7 = 14, then add 1 to get 15. Don't forget that extra 1.

questions.question: Maya has 3 red apples and 3 green apples. How many apples in all?
questions.explain: 3 + 3 is a double. Two 3s make 6. Be careful not to count one extra or one short.

questions.question: Sam has 7 stickers on his shirt and 7 on his bag. How many stickers in all?
questions.explain: 7 + 7 is a double. Two 7s make 14. A common slip is picking 13 or 15, which are one off.

questions.question: To find 3 + 4, you start with 3 + 3 = 6. What do you do next?
questions.explain: 3 + 4 is one more than 3 + 3. So you add 1 to 6 to get 7. The trap is subtracting instead.

questions.question: Leo puts 4 cookies on one plate and 4 on another. How many cookies on both plates?
questions.explain: 4 + 4 is a double. Two 4s make 8. A common slip is writing 7 or 9, which are one off.

questions.question: Aisha has 5 shells. Her friend gives her 6 more. How many shells does Aisha have now?
questions.explain: 5 + 6 is a near double. Start with 5 + 5 = 10, then add 1 to get 11. The trap is stopping at 10.

questions.question: Two friends share 13 shells in all. One friend has 6. How many does the other have?
questions.explain: 6 + 7 = 13, so the other friend has 7. This is a near double: 6 + 6 = 12, add 1 to get 13.

questions.question: Nate has 9 cards. His brother has 8 cards. How many cards do they have together?
questions.explain: 9 + 8 is a near double. Think 8 + 8 = 16, then add 1 to get 17. Don't forget that extra 1.

questions.question: Noah knows 6 + 6 = 12. He uses it to find a missing number. What number goes in the blank: 6 + ? = 13
questions.explain: 13 is one more than the double 12, so the missing number is one more than 6, which is 7. Many kids keep 6 or drop to 5 instead of adding one.

questions.question: Tess has 6 stickers. Her friend gives her 7 more. Then her cousin gives her 1 more. How many stickers does Tess have now?
questions.explain: Use 6 + 6 = 12, then add 1 more to get 6 + 7 = 13. Then add the cousin's 1 sticker to make 14. The trap is stopping at 13 and forgetting the last sticker.

questions.question: Sam wants to add 8 + 9. He says 8 + 8 = 16, so 8 + 9 = 16. What should Sam fix?
options: Take away 1, because 9 is one less than 8.
Add 1 more, because 9 is one more than 8.
Add 2 more, because 16 is two too small.
questions.explain: 9 is one more than 8, so 8 + 9 is one more than 16, which is 17. Many kids stop at the double or take one away by mistake.

questions.question: Kai has 9 hockey cards. He wants 19 cards in all. How many more cards does he need?
questions.explain: Start from the double 9 + 9 = 18. 19 is one more than 18, so Kai needs one more card than 9, which is 10. The trap is answering 9 and forgetting that extra card.
